nodes.title: OpenAI Agents SDK: Running agents (max_turns, error_handlers)
Pydantic AI agent docs (usage_limits, usage=, interrupted response)

nodes.text: Pydantic-AI UsageLimits offers cost_limit (USD Decimal), request_limit, tool_calls_limit, input_tokens_limit, output_tokens_limit, total_tokens_limit and per_request_input_tokens_limit; all except request_limit default to None.

Pydantic-AI request_limit defaults to 50, and a default UsageLimits() is created when none is passed, so a request cap is ON by default (not zero-config opt-in). It counts model responses committed to history, not retries or fallback attempts. Setting a limit to None disables it.
nodes.limitations: Default value read from the docs page; the 'usage_limits or UsageLimits()' line came from a truncated read of agent/__init__.py (s9, skim).

nodes.text: Pydantic-AI enforces limits at two points: check_before_request (request count, and projected input/total tokens/cost) before each model call, and check_tokens after each response. Both raise the typed UsageLimitExceeded; tool-call limits use check_before_tool_call. H4 is confirmed on enforcement points.

Pydantic-AI pre-request token enforcement is opt-in: count_tokens_before_request=False by default, because it costs an extra token-counting call and is supported only for Anthropic, Google, Bedrock Converse and OpenAI Responses. Otherwise input/output/total token limits trip only after the response that crossed them (overshoot by one response).

When a Pydantic-AI limit trips, the run raises UsageLimitExceeded instead of returning a result, but the crossing response is kept in the run's captured messages with state='interrupted', so partial history is recoverable via capture_run_messages and can be resumed.
nodes.limitations: Interrupted-state quote comes from a truncated skim of the agent docs; the spend page confirms capture_run_messages holds the partial history.

nodes.text: Pydantic-AI UsageLimits is scoped to a single run(); a longer period needs the earlier usage carried in via the usage= parameter (a RunUsage accumulated across runs) or a harness SpendLimits capability. H4's per-conversation part is confirmed in mechanism, though the exact check-against-shared-usage semantics were read only from docs prose.

Pydantic AI Harness SpendLimits adds budgets (e.g. usd per window such as UTC day or run) with state persisting across runs. It gates before each request, records spend after each response, raises SpendLimitExceeded (a UsageLimitExceeded subclass), and can overshoot: the crossing request completes and concurrent runs can both pass the check.
nodes.limitations: Separate harness package, not core; overshoot is by design (post-hoc recording).

nodes.text: OpenAI Agents SDK has no token, cost or tool-call cap: usage is tracked per run for monitoring only, each Runner.run returns usage for that run alone, and sessions do not carry usage. Its only limit is max_turns (LLM calls in the loop) raising MaxTurnsExceeded; max_turns=None disables it. H5 confirmed for the SDK.
nodes.limitations: Docs-based; absence of a feature is inferred from docs not mentioning it.

nodes.text: OpenAI Agents SDK error_handlers (keys max_turns, model_refusal, invalid_final_output) let the host return a controlled final output instead of raising MaxTurnsExceeded; the fallback enters history and the session by default (include_in_history=True). RunResult.to_state() snapshots usage so a resumed run continues from those totals.

LangGraph caps only graph steps (super-steps) via config recursion_limit, raising GraphRecursionError; default 10,007 since 1.1.4 (10,000 for 1.0.6-1.1.3). It has no built-in token or cost limit, and the docs do not say what state is preserved when it trips. H5 confirmed.
nodes.limitations: Docs-based; absence of a token cap inferred. State on error unverified (middleware like ModelCallLimit exists in langchain but was not checked).

nodes.text: Design inference: a library should offer an opt-in limits object checked before each model call (request/step count, projected tokens/cost) and after each response, raising one typed exception that carries the partial messages, with a caller-owned usage accumulator passed between runs for conversation scope. Pydantic-AI is the closest model; its non-zero request_limit default and after-the-fact token checks are the weak points, and OpenAI/LangGraph offer only turn/step caps.
